title.narrative: BEST: Program for Empowering Youth and Religious Actors to Promote Tolerance and Diversity - JULY- DECEMBER 2022

description.narrative:
This progress narrative covers activities from July 1 to December 31, 2022. The first section of this report includes the country context, while the second section provides an account of this period’s successful program activities. Overall, this period achieved the outputs that it had anticipated. Under Objective #1, 140 people of youth and religious leaders have participated in mentoring activities with communities in several areas. From our observations, most of them have been involved in activities, and 78 people have shown a role in facilitating discussions, training, interfaith dialogue meetings, and campaigns.
For Objective #2, local forums have been established in three areas where interfaith actors meet to set up a strategy and agenda for local networks. The meeting is the starting point for a networking agenda in the regions that coordinates youth groups and religious leaders in managing diversity issues at the local level. A forum also has been held at a national level, where diversity activists from various regions have met and succeeded in formulating guidelines for the network, including management of the network, leadership for community organizers, advocacy methods, and values and principles in networking.
Under Objective #3, there has been interaction between youth from across religions through dialogue to build social trust and awareness of FoRB. There has also been engagement by interfaith actors to both state and non-state stakeholders to advocate diversity. Finally, under Objective #4, campaign content containing messages about “Different yet Equal” has been spread on social media by reaching 55.000 people with 1500 engagements on average. Youth and religious leaders have also participated in campaigns to promote tolerance and peace. Meanwhile, during this reporting period, the program has monitored online media reporting on cases of intolerance throughout 2022 as our initial stage in conducting studies to create policy briefs for the next reporting period.

title.narrative: The Document Narrative of Social Media Campaign

description.narrative: For the mainstreaming paradigm of FoRB in the Indonesian sociopolitical sphere, we have carried out a campaign with content production and dissemination of content through social media.

For the mainstreaming paradigm of FoRB in the Indonesian sociopolitical sphere, we have carried out a campaign with content production and dissemination of content through social media. YBAW appointed a team that has the experience and expertise to produce content, then we have distributed the content through the Gusdurian Network’s social media channels: YouTube, FaceBook, Instagram, and Twitter. GUSDURian Network have created content with the hashtag #BedaSetara starting with research on various issues of diversity on social media. We sorted out between strategic issues and actual issues that need to be responded to. Under strategic issues such as democracy and citizenship, tolerance, and human rights, we used the technique of mainstreaming issues by filling the social media space with alternative content and narratives. Meanwhile, on actual issues, namely events that were trending at that time, we responded by linking them to the alternative narrative “BedaSetara” that we were developing and creating a counter narrative

target.value: Social Media account of Youth and religious leader

comment.narrative: The Youth and Religious Leader practiced more campaign strategies by mainstreaming issues and developing alternative narratives because the public already has the same views regarding diversity.

actual.value: Social Media account of Youth and religious leader

comment.narrative:
During 2022, our team has produced 30 contents in the form of short videos (11 times), infographics (11 times), and threads (8 times). Out of all the content we have distributed, it has reached 55.000 people with 1500 engagements on average.
In addition to the campaign by the team, we encourage youth leaders and religious leaders who have gained a new perspective on diversity and FoRB through previous training to get involved in the campaign. In our observation, several youth leaders and religious leaders also carried out campaigns on social media with a total of 359 content distributed through various social media platforms throughout 2022. On Facebook, there are 112 youth leaders and religious leaders who are actively creating campaign content.
Meanwhile, there were 113 people who actively carried out campaigns via Instagram, and only 4 people who carried out campaigns via Twitter

title.narrative: The Document Narrative of Local Forum

description.narrative:
GUSDURian Network have facilitated several meetings to set up a strategy and agenda for local networks. The forum is formed jointly by a network of organizations or local communities to organize resources, design strategies, and carry out mutual planning regarding issues of diversity and tolerance. In the long term, the network will actively advocate for diversity and equality with sustainability.
GUSDURian Network have did 4 Local Forum on 4 communities, Banjarmasin, Pontianak, Semarang, and Surabaya.

Local Forum in Surabaya was held on 16 October 2022 at Asrama Haji in conjunction with the Gusdurian Network National Meeting, attended by 142 people (87 M, 55 F), consisting of religious leaders and community activists in the East Java region.

comment.narrative: Strengthening state actors and local communities with a perspective of justice and equality, preventing intolerance, and strengthening Human rights

The Forum has recommended for the government and parliament to expand democratic space by revising various regulations that are counterproductive to justice and guaranteeing equal living space, freedom of opinion, and expression.
The participants also urged the government to enforce laws that reflect justice and fulfillment of constitutional rights by addressing the violation of human rights, restoring the rights of the victim, preventing intolerance through regulations, and strengthening state actors with a perspective of justice and equality. The Forum also recommended all elements of civil society build a dialogue space for strengthening social cohesion to restore polarization in the grassroots communities.

description.narrative: The Forum in Banjarmasin was held on November 21, 2022, at the Dhammasoka Temple Hall in Banjarmasin. There were 30 people from 18 CSO organizations participated in the activity. They are representatives of interfaith leaders and community leaders in Banjarmasin

comment.narrative: The Local stakeholder and local community must be understanding about interfaith, ethnic, and community to conduct education about diversity

This local meeting resulted in an understanding between stakeholders about the importance of increasing spaces for interfaith, ethnic, and cultural meetings so that groups can understand each other’s differences. The Forum also emphasized the need to encourage the role of government institutions such as FPK and FPUB to go down to the community to conduct education about diversity.

description.narrative: The forum was held at Pura Agung Giri Nata Semarang on 22 November 2022. The participants were interfaith leaders and youth from religious-based organizations in Semarang. There were 30 people, 28 male, and 2 (two) females, who attended the forum. Tedi Kholiludin, a lecturer at Wahid Hasyim University and a social worker at ELSA (Institute of Social and Religious Studies), guided this forum.

comment.narrative: The Local stakeholder and local community must be understanding about interfaith, ethnic, and community to conduct education about diversity

The discussion deliberated on the work of interfaith that had existed in the last five years, including achievements, current challenges, and joint plans for the coming years. The forum noted that the cross-faith network in the Semarang region has succeeded in stemming the movement of intolerant groups, promoting values of diversity, and advocating for the establishment of places of worship and religious celebrations for minority groups. As a result, there is no manifest rejection of diversity activities like in the previous cases of violations. People have begun to be open to differences in the city.
However, the participants also realized that the role of young people in activities is minimum regarding the issues of diversity. So that, each religious group involved in the network should encourage their youth to be more active involvement in dialogue, advocacy, and campaign activities. Young groups must build interactions in interfaith activities more intensively. The meeting also recommended a need for mentoring for young people and delivering assistance for religious minority groups, and the involvement of women’s groups to build actor regeneration.

description.narrative: The forum was held on 23 November 2022 at the Meeting Hall of the Pontianak Deputy Mayor’s Office House, attended by 35 people, 27 men and 8 (eight) women from 22 organizations from various religions and ethnicity in Pontianak. Mohamad, the coordinator of Gusdurian in Pontianak, guided the discussion of the meeting.

comment.narrative: The Local stakeholder and local community must be understanding about interfaith, ethnic, and community to conduct education about diversity

actual.value: Interfaith Leaders, Community Leaders, and ethnic Organizations

comment.narrative: The Deputy Mayor of Pontianak expressed his support for the forum that brought together religious, faith, and civil mass organization leaders. Pontianak is a city that has various ethnicities and religions, so collaboration between religious leaders is needed to create a city that is tolerant and conducive to living together. The meeting agreed on the need for massive positive narratives related to diversity in Pontianak so that negative sentiments do not occur between adherents of religions and ethnic groups, especially to anticipate identity-based conflicts in the political year. The forum also encourages the government to schedule the creation of a regional regulation on tolerance for community life in Pontianak in the local legislation program (Prolegda) in 2023.

comment.narrative: Discuss contemporary issues of tolerance and democracy with speakers, network management, community standard, advocacy methods, values, and principles in networks.

actual.value: Local Community of GUSDURian Network, activist, religious Leader

comment.narrative:
GUSDURian Network discussed contemporary issues of tolerance and democracy with speakers, then discussed network management, community standard, advocacy methods, values, and principles in networks in several groups, then we presented the results in a plenary session to get feedback. The division of groups and discussion points are as follows.
a. Discussion group on ethical principles. There were 89 people participated in this discussion. They agreed that communities and individuals involved in managing a community for the issue of tolerance need to apply nine principles, including integrity, anti-discrimination, independence, transparency, anti-violence, gender justice, partiality to marginalized groups, anti-oppression, and an ecological perspective. b. Group discussion on network management involved 68 people (55 male, 13 female). The group agreed on several principles in the network, including building public trust and credibility, respecting others; honest and open communication; high expectations and achievements; complying with the law or not committing a crime; avoiding conflicts of interest; loyalty to the value of equality and justice. c. Group discussion on leadership in the community. The forum involved 128 people (81 male, 47 female) in a conversation on a prototype of a cadre and leader for the community. The discussion has defined cadre as young people who have a strong commitment and are confident, responsible, tolerant, honest, inclusive, caring, fair, and open-minded. While leaders are people who have capacities, competence, integrity, walk the talk, have personal maturity, and have alignment with marginal groups. A leader has several characteristics, including independence, sovereignty, and loyal to values. They have competence in advocacy, able to inspire and drive change, have the critical thinking, and can produce knowledge. d. Group discussion on advocacy and community assistance. People involved in the group, 21 male and 12 female, agreed that advocacy needs to apply four approaches: 1) Right base approach through paying attention to “fulfilment of basic rights” in advocating public policy. 2) Respect base approach by paying attention to “respect for local values and wisdom” in advocating and assisting the community; 3) Resilience base, which means the community must strengthen the grassroots community. 4) Faith base approach, namely the use of values from religion and local wisdom such as humanity, justice, equality, liberation, simplicity, brotherhood, and traditional wisdom to support advocacy.

title.narrative: The Document Narrative of Interfaith Dialogue at Local Level

description.narrative: Interfaith dialogue is a meeting between religious groups facilitated by youth or religious leaders either in the visiting or meeting format to build trust and strengthen respect for differences. This activity aims to establish space for inter-religious interaction for building social trust and awareness of FoRB.

Interfaith dialogue in Semarang was on December 6, 2022, at the Faculty of Economics, Semarang State University. Interfaith activists at the local level attended this activity, as well as student organizations. The total number of participants is 80 (50 male and 30 female), consisting of 60% Muslim, 20% Protestant, and 20% Catholic. The dialogue brought out students from different faith base organizations backgrounds, such as
Catholic (Jesuit Union, Catholic Student Union), Muslim (KAMMI, HMI, PMII, IPNU- IPPNU), and other student organizations (BP2M, KMB, Eksis, Sindhat Joglo, Razam)

comment.narrative: To build trust and strengthen respect for differences

This dialogue discusses the issue of discrimination faced by minority groups on campus. Students from Muslim groups have easier access to campus facilities, and minority students face difficulty carrying out religious activities on campus.
The dialogue resulted in an understanding of the need to open spaces for diversity and harmony on campus. Students as young people must be able to become promoters for their generation in campaigning for a just and inclusive life.

description.narrative: The interfaith dialogue in Surabaya happened at Asrama Haji Surabaya on 14 October 2022. People from faith-based communities in East Java attended this event. The meeting discussed the religious moderation program, the policies of the Ministry of Religion, and its strategy and implementation at the local level. The discussion brought Marzuki Wahid from the Fahmina Institute and Lukman Hakim Saifudin, former Minister of Religion, as resource persons.

comment.narrative: To build trust and strengthen respect for differences.

The Discussion is about Religious Moderation. Religious moderation regulates that the majority can live more fairly with the minority. Meanwhile, Lukman Hakim Saifuddin emphasized that religious moderation is not only for Islamic groups but all religions. The government released the program to respond to several challenges: firstly, the phenomenon of religiosity that denies the universal values of religions resulted in an exclusive attitude.
Second, the emergence of extreme religious interpretations that reduce and distort human values. Third, the threat against national building due to practices of religion that damage and tear national ties. Majoritarianism is intolerable. Everyone has the right to be treated fairly and equally in religious life and everyday life. At this point, religious moderation needs to be practiced by all groups. People should avoid extreme attitudes toward diversity, Lukman said.

description.narrative: This activity was on November 19-20, 2022, at the Shantikara Youth Center Dormitory. The dialogue involved 39 youths (19 female and 20 male) from interfaith communities consisting of 13 Muslims, 19 Catholics, 6 Protestants, and 1 Hindu, including the GUSDURian Community of Yogyakarta, Srikandi Crossfaith (SRILI) that is an interfaith community, the Grigak Volunteer Community, the Syantikara Youth Center Students, and the Bantul Garbage Bank Community.

comment.narrative: To build trust and strengthen respect for differences

the activity began with the screening of a documentary film Luka Beta Rasa inspired by the conflict in Ambon. The film reflected how sensitive religion is when a negative narrative twisted it for the sake of a sectarian interest. Furthermore, participants discussed how to manage the issue of diversity to maintain peace amidst differences in religion, ethnicity, race, and culture.

title.narrative: The Interim Narrative Program - Mentoring for Youth and Religious Leader

description.narrative: The mentoring activities have been in 17 locations in several regions, including East Java, West Java, Central Java, Sulawesi, and Kalimantan, involving 204 people (147 male & 57 female) including youth leaders, religious leaders, and the community organizer

title.narrative: Mentoring for Youth and Religious Leader

description.narrative:
The learning process in mentoring sessions is to increase understanding of issues, community organizing, and how to build networks for diversity issues. In addition to providing knowledge about leadership as community organizers, the process is to map stakeholders for strengthening social movements based on diversity issues and mainstreaming the value of equality in society.
Using an appreciative inquiry approach, the facilitator guides the participants to build a personal vision as community leaders by exploring their potential and experiences, defining dreams, then identifying strategies to realize these dreams in the community, and analyzing actors who can support them. After that, the facilitator guides the participants’ discussion to identify challenges and opportunities at the local level. In each mentoring activity, the facilitator also conveys knowledge about leadership as a provision for managing the community. In the stakeholder mapping session, they analyzed the interests and influences of these stakeholders. In the final stage, participants formulated an action plan after the meeting. The lesson learned from this activity is that managing diversity issue requires convergence with other issues such as social justice, democracy, ecology, and education. Integrating these various issues can provide alternatives to manage tolerance and peace in society.

description.narrative: This forum aimed to discuss how to strengthen FoRB and diversity between interfaith networks and stakeholders at the local level. The meeting facilitated interfaith actors to engage with state and non-state actors to advocate diversity. After the forum, a collaboration among interfaith groups in dialogue and advocacy in disseminating the principles of Freedom of Religion and Belief (FoRB) will become even stronger. During this period, we have held three stakeholder forums, namely in Makassar, Gorontalo, and Surabaya.

The multi-stakeholder forum in Gorontalo was held on 7 November 2022 at the hall of the Ministry of Religion of Gorontalo City, attended by 34 people from representatives of government and non-government institutions. From the government, there were Misnawaty S. Nuna (Chairman of the Gorontalo City Ministry of Religion), Matris Luku (Head of Gorontalo City Government Welfare Unit), Mohamad Nasir Yasin (Head of the Gorontalo Police Intelligence Socio-Cultural Unit), Indriawan (Kodim 1304 Gorontalo), Burhanuddin Umar (Chairman of the Gorontalo Religious Harmony Forum), as well as representatives from the National Unity and Politics Unit (Kesbangpol) and the Gorontalo City Education Office. While from non-governmental organizations: Abdul Rasyid Kamaru (Tuan Qodhi), Abdul Muin Moduto (Alkhairat), Nanang Supriatna (Ahmadiyah), Arrang Batara (Ahlul Bait Indonesia, Pastor Iggi Prater (Catholic Church), Rev. Welly Rempy (Adventist Church), Pandita Waluyo Dwi Asmoro (Buddhist Dharma Indonesia Foundation), and several activists from the Gusdurian Network of Sulawesi.

comment.narrative: The Local government aware about how to strengthen FoRB and diversity between interfaith networks and stakeholders at the local level

This meeting was the first forum in Gorontalo, where various elements from the government and religion-based representatives gathered, including the Ahmadiyah group and the government. Samsi Pomalingo, a lecturer at Gorontalo State University and an alumnus of the religious leader workshop, facilitated the discussion. The meeting identified the discrimination against minority groups such as Ahmadiyah, Buddhists, and Christians, especially in building houses of worship. The head of the Ministry of Religion and the Gorontalo Government Welfare Unit appreciated this meeting. All participants hoped that all elements could collaborate regardless of background, build a common encounter space, and join hands to discuss diversity issues in Gorontalo in an inclusive

description.narrative: The stakeholder forum in Makassar was held on 5 November 2022 at the hall of the Makassar Religious Research and Development Center. There were 17 people who attended, and Saprillah Syahrir, Head of the Makassar Religious Research and Development Center, hosted this forum. Various representatives of government agencies were present, including Zainal Ibrahim, Head of the Makassar City Kesbangpol Agency, and Muhammad Tonang from the Ministry of Religion of Makassar City, Kombes Pol. Budhi Haryanto Makassar Police Chief, Usman Arsyad, Head of the National Assimilation Forum (Forum Pembauran)

comment.narrative: The local stakeholder aware about how to strengthen FoRB and diversity between interfaith networks and stakeholders at the local level.

All stakeholders were aware that Makassar is a barometer for eastern Indonesia, a city where people from various regions gather and meet for study, trade, or just transit. Its inhabitants come from diverse religions and ethnicities and live hereditary. There is often friction between ethnic groups due to the lack of space for intense dialogue and education. So, each group knows each other and understands the differences, especially in facing the political year. The forum also recommended a massive campaign on tolerance and countering the narratives of violence circulated in Makassar to mitigate conflict due to hatred between groups.

description.narrative: There were around 335 people (228 M, 107 F) that gathered in Asrama Haji Surabaya on 15 October 2022. They come from government agencies, such as the Head of Public Relations of the Regional Police, the Head of the Regional Ministry of Religion, religious leaders, local community leaders, and representatives of the Gusdurian network community from several regions in East Java.

comment.narrative: The local Stakeholder aware about how to strengthen FoRB and diversity between interfaith networks and stakeholders at the local level.

In this meeting, Jay Akhmad, Gusdurian’s Coordinator, conveyed several initiatives that Gusdurian Network had carried out, such as Gus Dur’s Thought Class, a leadership workshop for diversity; campaigns to deal with negative narratives on social media, and providing community assistance such as assisting in cases of refusal of places of worship to moving graves of different religions. Because Gusudurian is facing challenges, it needs cooperation from various parties. There were two recommendations from the meeting: firstly, the Network should continue its efforts to advocate for diversity, including assisting the construction of houses of worship and public cemeteries and preventing exclusivism and extremism. Secondly, the government should support the Network’s efforts to manage diversity.
